reviews.text: [h2] So based on the first couple of hours playing... [/h2] The game I can assure you this is worth getting. Compared to Shadow Corridor 1 it has: 1. [b] Better Plot, [/b] Won't spoil anything but it is much more concrete than the last game while building upon some smaller aspects within the Shadow Corridor universe. It provides a lot more context and lore when compared to the last game and requires (I know some people care about this) a lot less reading notes when compared to the first game. 2. [b] Better Graphics, [/b] This is a given to be honest considering the timing of this release compared to the last. 3. [b] Better Gameplay, [/b] My main gripe with the last game was the fact challenger difficulty on some levels would have numerous of the same apparitions and they could easily gang up on you regardless of how careful you are. In this game challenger difficulty feels more relaxed, less "apparition spamming" and most of all doesn't actually require you to play the harder difficulties to get the whole story unlike the last game. Also the good thing about the gameplay is it is a mix of being more experienced over time while playing and getting better cards while merely playing levels which helps the player throughout the game. This is done via the souls and magatama currencies within the game. And if you die you consume candles to keep you alive to finish the level (assuming you have candles left within the level). Another side note, you can use the skeletons as points of reference when traversing the corridors which should help those with navigation issues. [h2] Some points to improve on.. [/h2] Thus far I've only encountered three problems with the game: 1. [b] Dying (ironic right?), [/b] When you die an apparition can spawn pretty much on top of you so stay vigilant when and if you do die in a level since there's almost no grace period. 2. [b] Visual bugs, [/b] Sometimes when an action is performed at an inconvenient time (i.e pausing the game) lighting or visual effects will take place when they shouldn't be. 3. [b] The Compass Item, [/b] The compass seems to be having functionality issues once collected as I couldn't even use it in the first level. Other than that haven't found anything game breaking. Highly recommend.

Here's my revised review after all cleared and lingering around Deluge difficulty, marathons, etc for 200hrs Gameplay-wise, the difficulty went up significantly after the recent updates. Seems like the developer is pissed off at the reviews claiming how absurd it is to see the real ending. And there, let's make it more difficult to punish them. Now you have the nightmare following you from the first magatama in Deluge. I managed to clear after some retries and also in the marathon, but this feels stupid. But Tree complex is more crazy. You got ton of unavoidable traps, exploding dumplings that take your hp, can't even run which is absurd, and rain. Terribly balanced and this stage needs significant rework. Scariness-wise, I still don't get why they chose that audio for the running apparition. Not scary at all and feels extremely annoying. Feels like some mentally-disabled man throwing a tantrum, and you're forced to sit in a same room with him. Even after 200hrs of playing, I still can't get used to this thing. Framerate is unlocked after the recent update and it looks good. However, there're still some bugs where some karutas say it can't be sealed, but it gets sealed. Still a lot of bugs where apparitions get stuck and not move. Also a stuck isolated room too.

真结局神树关卡的解锁条件是：上级难度全部9个关卡通关后，会解锁腐花难度（只有一条命，死了就重来），是的，再重新把这9个关卡的腐花难度通关才能解锁神树关卡，简直累死人，影廊一真结局条件是4个勾玉关一命不死拿到金勾玉，而影廊2却要一命不死地通关8个收集勾玉关卡，其中第八关路还特别不好走，找齐勾玉还要花特别长的时间找出口，第三关的路极其相似，让人迷路，树海那关找齐勾玉后还会让区域内指南针失效，体力恢复大幅度下降，感觉没必要设计这么坐牢的结局解锁条件，我觉得如果不是影廊一爱好者，深度老手，不建议多次挑战关卡，极其的耗时间，加上bug真的很多，虽然作者修的也十分的积极，但你能接受收集完4个勾玉后，突然卡在某个界面强制重来的崩溃吗。 本作比上一作玩法更加丰富，简单来说就是将一的成就拆分成了卡牌和咖啡，卡牌的效果丰富多样，为关卡过关提供了各种便利，徘徊者和上一作也较相似 渦之舞者：旋转前进，有全方位视角的神乐铃，听力和视力范围一般，可以听见玩家的跑步声。 晴天娃娃：相当于一代的大队长，只有前方视力，对玩家跑步声音不敏感。 紫怨: 相当于一代的哭鬼，完全没有视力，听力范围很小，但听觉相当敏感，可以听见玩家的走路声并触发追击，比一代哭鬼更加敏感，光是走路几步就会触发追击。 蛟女:相当于一代的无声和老头，以地面上的一滩水进行无声移动，听到玩家或者鞭炮的声音会快速靠近，变成鬼形态需要数秒时间，玩家可以利用这段时间逃脱。 机械人偶: 只在祭殿一关出现，相当难缠。普通难度下所有机械人偶都在站岗，当其眼前亮起灯光时，玩家不能通过，否则会激活人偶并触发追击，人偶没有听觉，但视力极好。不过可以被必经之路上的鞭炮挡住，普通难度和困难难度下，玩家拿到第三个勾玉和第五勾玉的时候，所有的人偶会激活一段时间，不过只在站岗地方的周围巡逻，不敢过的话可以躲到柜子里等到人偶全部归位。在此之前被激活的任务是不会归位的，除非玩家死亡。 新潮女士: 头部长有留声机的幽灵，没有视力，听力较好，可以利用声波锁定正前方的玩家，一旦玩家被锁定会直接触发追击，其声波还有让玩家疯狂的功效，除非用鞭炮或者躲到柜子里。 秽人: 初次出现在第三关，普通难度下，玩家拿到第三个和第五个勾玉的时候，会全屏刷出大量秽人，可以自动追踪玩家，被抓住需要挣脱并会持续扣血，而且会在一局内永久封印玩家的一项卡牌。可以用鞭炮大范围驱散或者手枪单独打散。

手动解锁帧率的办法：在[i]C:\Users\[用户名]\AppData\Local\ShadowCorridor2\Saved\Config\Windows [/i]中找到 [i]GameUserSettings [/i]，用文本编辑器打开，找到[b] FrameRateLimit [/b] 的配置，改为 [b]FrameRateLimit=360 [b]，后面的数字是你想限制到的帧数。修改完记得保存，然后将此文件改为只读。 To manually unlock the frame rate: find [i]GameUserSettings [/i] in [i]C:\Users\[username]\AppData\Local\ShadowCorridor2\Saved\Config\Windows [/i], open it up with a text editor and find the [b] FrameRateLimit [/b] configuration, change it to [b]FrameRateLimit=360 [b], the number after that is the number of frames you want to limit it to. Remember to save it after modifying it, and then make this file read-only.

Typical experience is : You arrive in a new level. You walk around, search for items and look for objectives while listening to sounds. As you progress into the level, you recognize some ennemies and identify new threats you haven't encountered before. You start to learn and experiment with the new threats. Progressing carefully, you're always on the edge because you can't simply respawn; death has a meaning (restarting the entire level once you're out of lives) so you cannot afford to get careless. If you perish, all is not lost because you've learned valuable information and you can choose some temporary buffs for your next attempt. Overall, the game is excellent. You can replay the same levels in different difficulties without getting bored chasing a higher score, trying a different "build" or just enjoying the experience. There is a lot to do and it doesn't get old. I'll probably try to 100% the game if achievements are reasonnables. You cannot rebind the movement keys so you'll have to change your keyboard to qwerty if needed. In 1.07+ I haven't encountered any bugs and the performances are good (Ryzen 7 5800, rtx3070 laptop)

Ugh...I don't want to give a 'not recommended', but I don't like the directions the changes went towards compared to the first game. So I'll start with the good, and I'm playing on Intermediate/Normal difficulty. Good: - Updated graphics and UI look really nice. - Unique Stages - More apparitions! - More items - The base area, cards/karuta system, and coffee buffs are pretty neat - General gameplay loop plays the same as the first game Bad: - Procedural Generation in this one is too random? The first game also had random generation, but had static areas, which acted as landmarks for your character. This game doesn't have that luxury and leads to being extremely lost as you continue to run into areas very early and frequently that look identical to one another, sometimes not even minutes apart. You can drop stones but those are rng dependent. Knowing the gameplay loop, I ended up taking 3hrs to complete the area due to the layout added to the already massive amount of rng in the game. - Magatama spawns seem more limited than the first game. On it's own its fine, but when combined with everything else, it becomes frustrating. I.E. there is only 1 magatama in viewing distance using clairvoyance but it requires a key, that you don't have? Better hope it drops nearby and that you remember that exact room location that's identical to the rooms parallel to it if/when you do find one. - Some cards/items need tweaking. Minimap display should have a toggle for on off, or at least a 'minimum souls for activation' sort of thing. Automatic Door is broken and immediately closes upon you when used, you can't through the door before it closes in your face, leaving it useless in emergency situations. The shrine that gives you the extra candle should give you the extra life. Why does it have to be used in another randomly generated area??? The Hourglass SUCKS! I've used it a few times, but with the crying child, she instantly tracks you afterwards no matter how far you run while time is stopped. This is personal, but the two-hold candle shouldn't be able to be extinguished once lit, nor should it be able to use your last life. Because when you're using the controller, sometimes when bringing up the items, it defaults to the light source instead of your items, and causes your light source to extinguish. - Traps were a good idea in theory, but the execution is really disappointing. Unfortunately, it's only a couple of traps so far I've run into that make me wanna quit. Floor trap is simple enough, no problems. Hanging trap you'll always get got by it no matter what. Insanity Gauge? I've never been able to run away from the sound, or find a space to hide in afterwards. It fills up super fast, and your chain smoking teen is already out of stamina by the time the gauge is half filled. Worse mechanic I've gotten to so far has to be the Corruption Gauge though. I literally died at 5 magatama with compass because I couldn't find a corpse to heal my corruption level, so it filled up. I died looking for the alter to complete the level after an hour in the stage. - Shop keeper. He doesn't sell all the rng items! I needed a key for a room, and so used my ticket to get to him only to find out that he didn't even HAVE any strange keys. Additionally, when warping out, I ended up in front of the crying child TWICE in two different levels(who aggro'd immediately)! What is the point of going to the shopkeep if he ends up not having any items that would help you find things faster?? That's all I have for now, which is also why i can't really recommend this game currently. The heavy RNG for literally everything in game makes for an experience in frustration. You'll get lucky and get out relatively quickly; or you'll get unlucky and it'll be a slog of dodging apparition after apparition to find the items you need.

The sequel brought a lot of new playstyles and features that the first game did not have, but suffers similar problems from the first game. The levels are much more diverse with each one having its signature monsters and others that carry over into the lower levels. The introduction of karuta cards is a great and welcome new feature to the franchize that adds new various effects, items, and abilties that can help your future corridor runs, or even change item effects to empower you. the pros of this game is that it excells at being a random generated labarynth survival horror, while the first game may have been random in level design, the specific rooms needed for secrets or magatamas were made with a tileset. This was generally fine flaw, as it provided level stability and detailed areas. The second game embraces the randomizer to the fullest, as each time I play the game, the level feels absolutely unrecognizable each time you play. The generation in the sequel feel smore polished than the first. the levels also tend to have windows that lead to a skybox, dont trust the windows. these are decievingly effective usage to confuse the player, as the window may have a hallway behind it. and fun fact, the deeper the levels you go and see those windows, the higher you are. Another feature that is impressive is that each level is unique in adding debuffs to hinder your exploration. From spawning enemies, to changing the dungeon's rules. Compared to the first game, it rewarded you for kokeshi completion and completing levels on progressively harder difficulty to unlock starting items, easter egg items, and level effects. in the sequel, the game remembers how many overall magatama you collect and can be traded for karuta cards which unlock new various playstyles that the first game restricted to items only and not statistics, passives, item buffs/combos. The first game was pure survival horror, what you find in the level is what you get. In the new game, interactable objects cacn give you souls, which can fuel items you obtain, or can be traded at hotaruya for new items. This place is a lifesaver on higher difficulties while the first game punished you for using items subpar. If you dont want to use hotaruya, you can turn off music in settings, which in turn makes the game even more scary. The cons are that despite the new monsters, some old too if you buy the dlc, they have audio-loops which can be really irritating after 40+ hours of gameplay, or being pinned in a location because there are too many apparitions around. The sound effects or much diverse than the first game, but are still repetitive. I greatly appreciate the concept of a 3rd release of shadow corridor, but the monsters really need to have various audio tracks to keep them unique. Compared to the first game, the crying woman was particularly irritating when moving or suspecting the player is near. Multiple monsters in the sequel have the same problem but have longer, more various noises that are an improvement. A couple of monsters in the new game are reskins of monsters from the last game, though not bad on itself, made it feel easy to avoid most of them from the start. I really would have liked more variance in apparitions the higher difficulty you play on, and instead of reskinned monsters, bring back the ones from the past with better graphics, and focus on new ones that are exclusive on higher difficulties or levels. I have unlocked the 100 coffee bean drink, but the perk explanation is bizzare and I've never managed to activate it, yet at least. To be fair, SpaceOnigiri games is an indie company, and I can only begin to comprehend the difficulty of making a game single handed, but considering the limitations, it is an impressive overhaul compared to the first and I would recommend this game more than the first for its variation and ease of access to new and old players. In closing, I absolutely reccomend this game if you are a fan of Japanese aesthetics, labarynth horror, and are looking for a spooky, but welcoming game. Shador corridor is one of the few horror games that feels equally comforting as it is scary. If you are willing to forgive its indie limitations and see the game for its essence rather than its looks, it is an experience that will make you keep playing. I plan to 100% the game and the first, but its not easy. If there was a shadow corridor 3, I hope they get a larger development team to really give it their all. I've loved this game franchize since it launched, and I plan to stay tuned if there is anymore dlc or sequels. I hope that if a third game is released, it combines what made the first and second game amazing; from items, monsters, level design, everything. Or maybe new monsters that have more distinct abilities and ways to get around them. I hope if there is dlc or a third game, they add even more levels, even if its legacy levels from the past games. I understand thats an overly-ambitious request but I think SpaceOnigiri games can do it. I have faith in them.

This game is in most aspects an upgrade compared to Shadow Corridor 1, but I'd also like to mention a caveat here. I do overall recommend this game, because it's got: - Better graphics - More items, mechanics, and apparitions - Something akin to a world hub with customization options built into the experience instead of in options menus - A more coherent story (though, I don't think the story in Shadow Corridor 1 was bad) - More levels, each with appealing themes to them The overall new experience is fresh enough, plays nicely enough, and provides enough of a challenge with the medals system that I think people coming from SC1 will like this game. However, it's of course inevitable that people who play this game will make comparisons to SC1. "Is Shadow Corridor 2 better?" It's a question with some hidden assumptions baked in; for example, the assumption that the core gameplay is similar or improved upon. And to that I say, the way the dungeons are randomized is not strictly worse or better, it's simply different. If you come into this game thinking that it SHOULD feel similar to how exploration works in SC1, you might be disappointed. In SC1, after several hours of play you can come to recognize the ~25 or so layouts in each stage as you replay them, and notice certain patterns or landmarks as you traverse around and make a mental map of the maze as you explore. However, instead of entire rooms being handcrafted and randomized into a grid like SC1, SC2 has a grid system where within a block, there are several smaller rooms, which occasionally include certain landmarks or features in them, as well as other small side rooms with items and lamps in them, connected by randomized hallways. These sections are then arranged in a grid-like pattern similar to SC1. The randomization within the room blocks is a two-edged sword; on the one hand, it makes subsequent plays always feel different since nothing is recognizable from play to play. On the other hand, the lack of recognizable landmarks makes exploration more difficult (particularly if you're trying to go over everything with a fine-tooth comb, such as to collect the coffee beans), and I feel like the randomness within a room block makes the dungeon a feel a little less inspired to look at. Take for example, the Abyss from SC1. It's got immediately recognizable, iconic rooms to it. The room with the lever puzzle leading to a hidden kagura. The room with the lever and a floor that falls away leading to the secret exit. The 3-floor maze room with the long hallways, rubbish piles, and stairs on the sides. The room with the bridge that goes across the top with a magatama under it, and the kagura bursts out when you approach. All of these rooms are immediately and distinctly recognizable, as well as completely hand-crafted, and each one feels like a cohesive experience that the room is trying to present to the player; more so than what you might encounter in a typical room block in SC2 due to the smaller size of the side rooms. So, I err on the side of saying that I generally prefer exploration of the dungeons more in SC1, but not so much so that I would say SC2 is bad; it's not, and I have greatly enjoyed what I've experienced so far playing SC2. I am going to continue and try to go for 100% in SC2! So to answer the question of is SC2 better than SC1, I would say in its totality, yes. The only caveat is the way dungeons are generated, but even that, in my opinion, just causes SC1 to not lose replay value. Like, consider for a moment what the replayability situation is like for The Binding of Isaac. If you go on Reddit or YouTube to see people playing that game, no one plays the original any more these days; everyone's moved on to Rebirth, because it strictly added to the core systems in every way, so there's no reason to even play the original. But with how different dungeon generation is in SC2, I think SC1 provides a different enough experience that it is still worth playing as well from time to time, depending on what you're in the mood for.
